query: First sale customs valuation automotive supplier imports

statements.text: Miller & Chevalier works closely with importers in multi-tiered transactions to assess whether the first or an earlier sale can be used to establish the transaction value.

The First Sale Rule (FSR) allows U.S. importers to calculate customs duties based on the price paid in the first sale of goods intended for export to the United States, instead of the higher resale price paid by a middleman or distributor.

This rule is applicable when goods are imported in a multi-tiered transaction, such as when a foreign manufacturer (factory) sells goods to a foreign middleman that, in turn, sells the goods to a U.S. importer.
U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) looks to the entirety of the circumstances.

Over 30 years ago, the Federal Circuit in Nissho Iwai American Corp. v. United States, 982 F.2d 505 (Fed. Cir. 1992), accepted what is commonly known as the "First Sale Rule" for U.S. customs purposes.
